# 🦛 chonkiejs ✨

_🦛 CHONK your texts in TypeScript with Chonkie!✨ The no-nonsense lightweight and efficient chunking library._

[Installation](#-installation) •
[Usage](#-usage) •
[Chunkers](#chunkers) •
[Acknowledgements](#acknowledgements) •
[Citation](#citation)

</div>

We built `chonkiejs` while developing a TypeScript web app that needed fast, on-the-fly text chunking for RAG applications. After trying several existing libraries, we found them either too heavy or not flexible enough for our needs. `chonkiejs` is a port of the original `chonkie` library, but with some type-safety and a few extra features to make it more useful for TypeScript developers!

**🚀 Feature-rich**: All the CHONKs you'd ever need </br>
**✨ Easy to use**: Install, Import, CHONK </br>
**⚡  Fast**: CHONK at the max speed of TypeScript! tssssooooooom </br>
**🪶 Light-weight**: No bloat, just CHONK </br>
**🦛 Cute CHONK mascot**: psst it's a pygmy hippo btw </br>
**❤️ [Moto Moto](#acknowledgements)'s favorite TypeScript library** </br>

**Chonkie** is a chunking library that "**just works**" ✨

> [!NOTE]
> This library is not a _binding_ but a _port_ of the original `chonkie` library written in Python, to TypeScript. This library is still under active development and not at feature parity with the original `chonkie` library yet. Please bear with us! 🫂

## 📦 Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core
```

## 📚 Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

// Create a chunker
const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 512
});

// Chunk your text
const chunks = await chunker.chunk('Your text here...');

// Use the chunks
for (const chunk of chunks) {
  console.log(chunk.text);
  console.log(`Tokens: ${chunk.tokenCount}`);
}
```

## 📦 Packages

| Package | Description | Dependencies |
|---------|-------------|--------------|
| [@chonkiejs/core](./packages/core) | Local chunking (Recursive, Token, Sentence, Semantic, Code, Table, Fast) with character-based tokenization | Zero |
| [@chonkiejs/cloud](./packages/cloud) | Cloud-based chunkers (Semantic, Neural, Code, etc.) via api.chonkie.ai | @chonkiejs/core |
| [@chonkiejs/token](./packages/token) | HuggingFace tokenizer support for core chunkers | @huggingface/transformers |

## Chunkers

All chunkers are available from `@chonkiejs/core` and follow the same pattern: `await ChunkerClass.create(options)` returns an instance, then `await chunker.chunk(text)` returns a `Chunk[]`.

### TokenChunker

Splits text into fixed-size token chunks with optional overlap.

```typescript
import { TokenChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await TokenChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 512,      // max tokens per chunk (default: 512)
  chunkOverlap: 50,    // overlapping tokens between chunks (default: 0)
  tokenizer: 'character', // tokenizer model name or Tokenizer instance (default: 'character')
});
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(text);
```

### RecursiveChunker

Recursively splits text using a hierarchy of rules: paragraphs → sentences → punctuation → words → characters. The most general-purpose chunker.

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 512,              // max tokens per chunk (default: 512)
  tokenizer: 'character',      // tokenizer model name or Tokenizer instance (default: 'character')
  minCharactersPerChunk: 24,   // min characters when merging splits (default: 24)
  // rules: RecursiveRules,    // custom split hierarchy (optional)
});
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(text);
```

### SentenceChunker

Groups sentences into token-sized chunks, respecting sentence boundaries.

```typescript
import { SentenceChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await SentenceChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 2048,                         // max tokens per chunk (default: 2048)
  chunkOverlap: 0,                         // overlapping tokens between chunks (default: 0)
  minSentencesPerChunk: 1,                 // min sentences per chunk (default: 1)
  minCharactersPerSentence: 12,            // min chars for a sentence (default: 12)
  delim: ['. ', '! ', '? ', '\n'],         // sentence boundary delimiters (default)
  includeDelim: 'prev',                    // attach delimiter to 'prev' | 'next' | 'none' (default: 'prev')
  tokenizer: 'character',
});
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(text);
```

### SemanticChunker

Detects natural chunk boundaries by computing embedding similarity between sliding sentence windows and splitting at low-similarity valleys.

```typescript
import { SemanticChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await SemanticChunker.create({
  embeddings: async (texts) => myModel.encode(texts), // required: (texts: string[]) => Promise<number[][]>
  // or:  embeddings: myModel,  // any object with .embed(texts) method
  chunkSize: 2048,             // max tokens per chunk (default: 2048)
  threshold: 0.8,              // similarity threshold for splits; lower = more splits (default: 0.8)
  similarityWindow: 3,         // sentences per sliding window embedding (default: 3)
  minSentencesPerChunk: 1,     // min sentences per chunk (default: 1)
  minCharactersPerSentence: 24,
  tokenizer: 'character',
});
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(text);
```

### CodeChunker

Splits source code into AST-aware chunks using [tree-sitter](https://tree-sitter.github.io/). Requires `web-tree-sitter` and a language grammar.

```typescript
import { CodeChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

// Using a language id (requires `tree-sitter-wasms` package)
const chunker = await CodeChunker.create({
  language: 'javascript',   // language id, .wasm path/URL, or Language instance
  chunkSize: 2048,
  tokenizer: 'character',
});
const chunks = chunker.chunk(sourceCode); // synchronous after create()
```

### TableChunker

Splits markdown or HTML tables into smaller sub-tables, each repeating the original header.

```typescript
import { TableChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

// Row mode (default): at most N data rows per chunk
const chunker = await TableChunker.create({
  tokenizer: 'row',  // 'row' for row-based, or any tokenizer for token-based (default: 'row')
  chunkSize: 3,      // max rows per chunk in row mode, max tokens in token mode (default: 3)
});
const chunks = chunker.chunk(markdownOrHtmlTable); // synchronous
```

### FastChunker

High-throughput byte-based chunker powered by WASM. Does not count tokens — suited for pre-processing or when speed matters most.

```typescript
import { FastChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await FastChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 4096,          // target chunk size in bytes (default: 4096)
  delimiters: '\n.?',       // boundary characters (default: '\n.?')
  // pattern: '---',        // multi-byte pattern (overrides delimiters)
  prefix: false,            // attach delimiter to start of next chunk (default: false)
  consecutive: false,       // split at start of consecutive delimiter runs (default: false)
  forwardFallback: false,   // search forward if no boundary found in backward window (default: false)
});
const chunks = chunker.chunk(text); // synchronous
```

# 🦛 Contributing to Chonkie

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

# 🦛 Contributing to Chonkie

> "I like them big, I like them CONTRIBUTING" ~ Moto Moto, probably

Welcome fellow CHONKer! We're thrilled you want to contribute to Chonkie. Every contribution—whether fixing bugs, adding features, or improving documentation—makes Chonkie better for everyone.

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Before You Dive In

1. **Check existing issues** or open a new one to start a discussion
2. **Read [Chonkie's documentation](https://docs.chonkie.ai)** and core [concepts](https://docs.chonkie.ai/getting-started/concepts)
3. **Set up your development environment** using the guide below

### Development Setup

```bash
# 1. Fork and clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs.git
cd chonkiejs

# 2. Install dependencies   
pnpm install
```

## 🧪 Testing & Code Quality

### Running Tests

```bash
cd packages/core
pnpm run test                              # Run all tests
pnpm vitest run tests/handshakes.test.ts   # Run specific test file
```

### Documentation Style

We follow Google-style docstrings:

```typescript
/**
 * Splits text into chunks of specified size.
 * 
 * @param text - Input text to chunk
 * @param chunk_size - Maximum size of each chunk
 * 
 * @returns List of text chunks
 * 
 * @throws ValueError if chunk_size <= 0
 */
function chunk_text(text: string, chunk_size: number): string[] {
    return text.split(' ').slice(0, chunk_size);
}
```

## 📦 Project Structure

```
packages/core/src/
├── types.ts          # Chunk class & shared types
├── tokenizer.ts      # Tokenizer abstraction
├── wasm.ts           # WASM initialization
├── recursive.ts      # RecursiveChunker
├── token.ts          # TokenChunker
├── fast.ts           # FastChunker (WASM byte-based)
├── sentence.ts       # SentenceChunker
├── semantic.ts       # SemanticChunker (embedding-based)
├── code.ts           # CodeChunker (tree-sitter)
├── table.ts          # TableChunker
├── handshakes/       # Vector DB wrappers
│   ├── base.ts       # BaseHandshake abstract class
│   ├── chroma.ts     # ChromaDB
│   ├── pinecone.ts   # Pinecone
│   ├── qdrant.ts     # Qdrant
│   ├── weaviate.ts   # Weaviate
│   ├── milvus.ts     # Milvus
│   ├── mongodb.ts    # MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
│   ├── elastic.ts    # Elasticsearch
│   ├── lancedb.ts    # LanceDB
│   ├── turbopuffer.ts # Turbopuffer
│   └── pgvector.ts   # pgvector (PostgreSQL)
```

## 🎯 Contribution Opportunities

### For Beginners

Start with issues labeled [`good-first-issue`](https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkie/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22)

### Documentation

- Improve existing docs
- Add examples or tutorials
- Fix typos

### Code Improvements

- Implement new chunking strategies
- Add tokenizer support
- Optimize existing chunkers
- Improve test coverage
- Bring to feature parity with Python library

### Performance Enhancements

- Profile and optimize code
- Add benchmarks
- Improve memory usage

### New Features

Look for issues with [FEAT] labels, especially those from Chonkie Maintainers

## 🚦 Pull Request Process

### 1. Branch Naming

- `feature/description` for new features
- `fix/description` for bug fixes
- `docs/description` for documentation changes

### 2. Commit Messages

Write clear, descriptive commit messages:

```
feat: add batch processing to WordChunker

- Implement batch_process method
- Add tests for batch processing
- Update documentation
```

### 3. Code Review

- **Make sure your PR is for the `development` branch**
- All PRs need at least one review
- Maintainers will review for:
  - Code quality
  - Test coverage
  - Performance impact
  - Documentation completeness

## 🦛 Technical Details

### Semantic Versioning

Chonkie does not follow strict semantic versioning. We follow the following rules:

- 'MAJOR' version when we refactor/rewrite large parts of the codebase
- 'MINOR' version when we add breaking changes (e.g. changing a public API)
- 'PATCH' version when we add non-breaking features (e.g. adding a new chunker) or fix bugs

# overview.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/api/overview.mdx

title: "API Overview"
description: "Complete API reference for @chonkiejs/core"

## Exports

```typescript
import {
  // Chunkers
  RecursiveChunker,
  TokenChunker,
  SentenceChunker,
  SemanticChunker,
  CodeChunker,
  TableChunker,
  FastChunker,

  // Utilities
  Chunk,
  Tokenizer,
  RecursiveRules,
  RecursiveLevel,
} from '@chonkiejs/core';
```

## Type Exports

```typescript
import type {
  RecursiveChunkerOptions,
  FastChunkerOptions,
  RecursiveLevelConfig,
  RecursiveRulesConfig,
  IncludeDelim,
} from '@chonkiejs/core';
```

## Common Patterns

### All chunkers share these methods:

| Method | Signature | Description |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| `chunk` | `(text: string) => Promise<Chunk[]>` | Chunk a single text |
| `chunkBatch` | `(texts: string[]) => Promise<Chunk[][]>` | Chunk multiple texts |

### Factory pattern (async creation):

All chunkers require async initialization via the static `create()` factory method:

```typescript
// All chunkers: RecursiveChunker, TokenChunker, SentenceChunker, SemanticChunker, CodeChunker, TableChunker, FastChunker
const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create(options);
```

# rules.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/api/rules.mdx

title: "RecursiveRules"
description: "Customizing the recursive chunking hierarchy"

## RecursiveRules

Defines the hierarchy of splitting rules for the `RecursiveChunker`.

### Default Rules

When no custom rules are provided, the default hierarchy is:

1. Paragraphs (`\n\n`, `\r\n`, `\n`, `\r`)
2. Sentences (`. `, `! `, `? `)
3. Punctuation (`{`, `}`, `(`, `)`, `,`, etc.)
4. Words (whitespace)
5. Characters (token-level fallback)

### Constructor

```typescript
import { RecursiveRules } from '@chonkiejs/core';

// Use default rules
const defaultRules = new RecursiveRules();

// Custom rules
const customRules = new RecursiveRules({
  levels: [
    { delimiters: ['\n\n'] },    // Paragraphs only
    { whitespace: true },         // Words
    {}                            // Characters (fallback)
  ]
});
```

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `levels` | `RecursiveLevel[]` | Array of chunking levels |
| `length` | `number` | Number of levels |

### Methods

#### `getLevel(index: number): RecursiveLevel | undefined`

```typescript
const firstLevel = rules.getLevel(0);
```

## RecursiveLevel

Represents one level in the recursive chunking hierarchy.

### Constructor

```typescript
import { RecursiveLevel } from '@chonkiejs/core';

// Split on newlines
const paragraphLevel = new RecursiveLevel({
  delimiters: ['\n\n', '\n']
});

// Split on sentence endings, keep delimiter with previous chunk
const sentenceLevel = new RecursiveLevel({
  delimiters: ['. ', '! ', '? '],
  includeDelim: 'prev'
});

// Split on whitespace
const wordLevel = new RecursiveLevel({
  whitespace: true
});

// Token level (no splitting, final fallback)
const tokenLevel = new RecursiveLevel();
```

### Options

| `delimiters` | `string \| string[]` | `undefined` | Delimiters to split on |
| `whitespace` | `boolean` | `false` | Use whitespace as delimiter |
| `includeDelim` | `'prev' \| 'next' \| 'none'` | `'prev'` | Where to include delimiter |

## Examples

### Code-optimized Rules

```typescript
const codeRules = new RecursiveRules({
  levels: [
    { delimiters: ['\n\n'] },           // Blank lines
    { delimiters: ['\n'] },             // Single lines
    { delimiters: [';', '{', '}'] },    // Statements
    { whitespace: true },                // Words
    {}                                   // Characters
  ]
});
```

### Markdown-optimized Rules

```typescript
const markdownRules = new RecursiveRules({
  levels: [
    { delimiters: ['\n## ', '\n# '] },  // Headings
    { delimiters: ['\n\n'] },            // Paragraphs
    { delimiters: ['. ', '! ', '? '] },  // Sentences
    { whitespace: true },                 // Words
    {}                                    // Characters
  ]
});
```

# tokenizer.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/api/tokenizer.mdx

title: "Tokenizer"
description: "Tokenizer interface and implementations"

## Character Tokenizer

The default tokenizer where 1 character = 1 token. Zero dependencies.

```typescript
import { Tokenizer } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const tokenizer = new Tokenizer();
```

### Methods

#### `countTokens(text: string): number`

```typescript
const count = tokenizer.countTokens('Hello'); // Returns 5
```

#### `encode(text: string): number[]`

```typescript
const tokens = tokenizer.encode('Hi'); // Returns [72, 105]
```

#### `decode(tokens: number[]): string`

```typescript
const text = tokenizer.decode([72, 105]); // Returns 'Hi'
```

#### `decodeBatch(tokensBatch: number[][]): string[]`

```typescript
const texts = tokenizer.decodeBatch([[72, 105], [66, 121, 101]]);
// Returns ['Hi', 'Bye']
```

## HuggingFace Tokenizer

For real token counting, install `@chonkiejs/token`:

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/token
```

```typescript
import { HuggingFaceTokenizer } from '@chonkiejs/token';

const tokenizer = await HuggingFaceTokenizer.create('gpt2');
const count = tokenizer.countTokens('Hello, world!'); // Real GPT-2 token count
```

## Using Tokenizers with Chunkers

Pass a tokenizer name when creating chunkers:

```typescript
import { TokenChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

// Character tokenizer (default, fast, zero deps)
const charChunker = await TokenChunker.create({
  tokenizer: 'character',
  chunkSize: 512
});

// GPT-2 tokenizer (requires @chonkiejs/token)
const gptChunker = await TokenChunker.create({
  tokenizer: 'gpt2',
  chunkSize: 512
});
```

# types.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/api/types.mdx

title: "Types"
description: "Core types and interfaces"

## Chunk

Represents a text chunk with metadata.

```typescript
class Chunk {
  text: string;       // The chunk text content
  startIndex: number; // Starting position in original text
  endIndex: number;   // Ending position in original text
  tokenCount: number; // Number of tokens in the chunk
}
```

### Constructor

```typescript
new Chunk(data: {
  text: string;
  startIndex: number;
  endIndex: number;
  tokenCount: number;
})
```

### Methods

#### `toString(): string`

Returns the chunk's text content.

```typescript
const chunk = new Chunk({
  text: 'Hello',
  startIndex: 0,
  endIndex: 5,
  tokenCount: 5
});

console.log(chunk.toString()); // 'Hello'
```

## RecursiveChunkerOptions

```typescript
interface RecursiveChunkerOptions {
  chunkSize?: number;              // Default: 512
  minCharactersPerChunk?: number;  // Default: 24
  rules?: RecursiveRules;          // Default: standard rules
  tokenizer?: Tokenizer | string;  // Default: character tokenizer
}
```

## FastChunkerOptions

```typescript
interface FastChunkerOptions {
  chunkSize?: number;          // Default: 4096
  delimiters?: string;         // Default: "\n.?"
  pattern?: string | Uint8Array;
  prefix?: boolean;            // Default: false
  consecutive?: boolean;       // Default: false
  forwardFallback?: boolean;   // Default: false
}
```

## RecursiveLevelConfig

```typescript
interface RecursiveLevelConfig {
  delimiters?: string | string[];
  whitespace?: boolean;
  includeDelim?: 'prev' | 'next' | 'none';
}
```

## IncludeDelim

```typescript
type IncludeDelim = 'prev' | 'next' | 'none';
```

# choosing-a-chunker.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/chunkers/choosing-a-chunker.mdx

title: "Choosing a Chunker"
description: "A guide to help you pick the right chunking strategy for your use case"

Not sure which chunker to use? This guide helps you pick the right one based on your use case, performance needs, and content type.

## Quick Recommendations

<Cards>
  <Card title="Building a RAG chatbot?" href="/chunkers/recursive-chunker">
    Use **RecursiveChunker** for general-purpose document chunking, or **SemanticChunker** if you need high topical coherence.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Processing source code?" href="/chunkers/code-chunker">
    Use **CodeChunker** — it understands AST structure and keeps functions/classes intact.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Need maximum throughput?" href="/chunkers/fast-chunker">
    Use **FastChunker** — high-performance byte-based chunking with SIMD acceleration.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Working with tabular data?" href="/chunkers/table-chunker">
    Use **TableChunker** — preserves headers and splits by rows.
  </Card>
</Cards>

## Decision Guide

Ask yourself these questions in order:

1. **Are you chunking source code?** → Use [CodeChunker](/chunkers/code-chunker)
2. **Are you chunking tables?** → Use [TableChunker](/chunkers/table-chunker)
3. **Is raw throughput your top priority?** → Use [FastChunker](/chunkers/fast-chunker)
4. **Do you need chunks grouped by topic?** → Use [SemanticChunker](/chunkers/semantic-chunker)
5. **Are simple sentence-boundary splits enough?** → Use [SentenceChunker](/chunkers/sentence-chunker)
6. **None of the above?** → Use [RecursiveChunker](/chunkers/recursive-chunker) (best default)

## Comparison Table

| Chunker | Speed | Quality | Dependencies | Best For |
|---------|-------|---------|--------------|----------|
| **FastChunker** | Fastest | Basic | None (SIMD) | High-throughput pipelines |
| **TokenChunker** | Very fast | Good | Tokenizer | Fixed-size chunks, token-based models |
| **SentenceChunker** | Fast | Good | Tokenizer | Clean sentence boundaries |
| **RecursiveChunker** | Fast | Very good | Tokenizer | General-purpose, structured docs |
| **TableChunker** | Fast | Excellent (tables) | None | Markdown/HTML tables |
| **CodeChunker** | Moderate | Excellent (code) | Tree-sitter | Source code files |
| **SemanticChunker** | Slower | Excellent | Embedding model | Topic-coherent chunks, RAG quality |

## When to Use Each

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### You just need it to work

    Start with **RecursiveChunker**. It's the best general-purpose option — fast, handles most document types well, and produces clean boundaries.

    ```typescript
    import { RecursiveChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

    const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
    const chunks = await chunker.chunk(text);
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### You need high-quality semantic chunks

    Use **SemanticChunker** with a custom embedding function. It groups sentences by meaning, so each chunk stays on-topic.

    ```typescript
    import { SemanticChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

    const chunker = await SemanticChunker.create({
      chunkSize: 512,
      threshold: 0.5,
      embeddings: async (texts) => { /* your embeddings */ }
    });
    const chunks = await chunker.chunk(text);
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### You're processing code

    Use **CodeChunker** — it parses the AST so your chunks respect function/class boundaries.

    ```typescript
    import { CodeChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

    const chunker = await CodeChunker.create({ language: 'typescript', chunkSize: 512 });
    const chunks = await chunker.chunk(sourceCode);
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### You need raw speed above all else

    Use **FastChunker** for pipelines where throughput matters more than boundary quality.

    ```typescript
    import { FastChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

    const chunker = await FastChunker.create({ chunkSize: 4096 });
    const chunks = await chunker.chunk(text);
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

## F.A.Q.

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="Can I switch chunkers without changing my pipeline?">
    Yes. All chunkers share the same async interface (`chunk()`, `chunkBatch()`). Swap one for another and everything downstream stays the same.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Should I use SemanticChunker or RecursiveChunker?">
    **RecursiveChunker** if you want speed and simplicity — it uses structural separators (newlines, periods, etc.) to find boundaries. **SemanticChunker** if retrieval quality is more important — it uses embeddings to keep semantically related content together, but requires an embedding function.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Is FastChunker good enough for RAG?">
    It depends on your tolerance for imperfect boundaries. FastChunker splits on byte counts, which can cut mid-word or mid-sentence. For RAG where retrieval quality matters, prefer RecursiveChunker or SemanticChunker.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

---

# code-chunker.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/chunkers/code-chunker.mdx

title: "CodeChunker"
description: "AST-aware chunking for source code"

The `CodeChunker` splits source code based on its abstract syntax tree (AST) structure, powered by tree-sitter. It understands code semantics and creates chunks that respect function/class boundaries.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { CodeChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await CodeChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 512,
  language: 'typescript'
});
```

## Parameters

| `chunkSize` | `number` | `512` | Maximum tokens per chunk |
| `language` | `string` | auto-detect | Programming language for AST parsing |
| `tokenizer` | `string` | `'character'` | Tokenizer to use |

## Supported Languages

The CodeChunker supports a wide range of languages via tree-sitter:

- JavaScript / TypeScript
- Python
- Rust
- Go
- Java
- C / C++
- Ruby
- And many more

## Usage

```typescript
import { CodeChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await CodeChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 512,
  language: 'typescript'
});

const code = `
function hello() {
  console.log("Hello, world!");
}

class Calculator {
  add(a: number, b: number): number {
    return a + b;
  }

  subtract(a: number, b: number): number {
    return a - b;
  }
}
`;

const chunks = await chunker.chunk(code);

for (const chunk of chunks) {
  console.log(`--- Chunk ---`);
  console.log(chunk.text);
  console.log(`Tokens: ${chunk.tokenCount}`);
}
```

# fast-chunker.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/chunkers/fast-chunker.mdx

title: "FastChunker"
description: "High-performance byte-based chunking"

The `FastChunker` provides high-performance byte-based chunking powered by `@chonkiejs/chunk`. Use it when you need delimiter/pattern boundary chunking with minimal overhead and don't need token-based limits.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { FastChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await FastChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 4096,
  delimiters: '\n.?',
  prefix: false,
  consecutive: false,
  forwardFallback: false
});
```

## Parameters

| `chunkSize` | `number` | `4096` | Target chunk size in bytes |
| `delimiters` | `string` | `"\n.?"` | Delimiter characters for boundary search |
| `pattern` | `string \| Uint8Array` | `undefined` | Multi-byte pattern to split on (overrides delimiters) |
| `prefix` | `boolean` | `false` | Put delimiter at start of next chunk instead of end of current |
| `consecutive` | `boolean` | `false` | Split at start of consecutive delimiter runs |
| `forwardFallback` | `boolean` | `false` | Search forward when no boundary found in backward window |

## Usage

```typescript
import { FastChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await FastChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 4096,
  delimiters: '\n.?'
});

const text = "First sentence. Second sentence. Third sentence.";
const chunks = chunker.chunk(text);

for (const chunk of chunks) {
  console.log(chunk.text);
  console.log(`Position: ${chunk.startIndex}-${chunk.endIndex}`);
}
```

<Callout type="info">
`FastChunker` always sets `tokenCount` to 0 on output chunks since it operates on bytes, not tokens.
</Callout>

## Batch Processing

```typescript
const batch = chunker.chunkBatch([
  'Document one...',
  'Document two...',
]);
```

---

# overview.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/chunkers/overview.mdx

title: "Chunkers Overview"
description: "Available chunkers in ChonkieJS"

ChonkieJS provides multiple chunking strategies for different text processing needs. All chunkers use an async `create()` factory and return `Promise<Chunk[]>` from their `chunk()` method.

<Callout type="info">
  Not sure which chunker to use? Check out the [Choosing a Chunker](/chunkers/choosing-a-chunker) guide for recommendations based on your use case.
</Callout>

## Available Chunkers

<Cards>
  <Card title="RecursiveChunker" href="/chunkers/recursive-chunker">
    Splits text hierarchically using customizable rules. Best for general-purpose chunking.
  </Card>
  <Card title="TokenChunker" href="/chunkers/token-chunker">
    Fixed-size token-based chunking. Best for consistent chunk sizes.
  </Card>
  <Card title="SentenceChunker" href="/chunkers/sentence-chunker">
    Splits at sentence boundaries. Preserves semantic completeness.
  </Card>
  <Card title="SemanticChunker" href="/chunkers/semantic-chunker">
    Groups content by semantic similarity using custom embeddings.
  </Card>
  <Card title="CodeChunker" href="/chunkers/code-chunker">
    AST-aware chunking for source code files.
  </Card>
  <Card title="TableChunker" href="/chunkers/table-chunker">
    Chunks markdown/HTML tables by row or token count.
  </Card>
  <Card title="FastChunker" href="/chunkers/fast-chunker">
    High-performance byte-based chunking with SIMD acceleration.
  </Card>
</Cards>

## Common Interface

All chunkers share these methods:

```typescript
// Chunk a single text
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(text);

// Chunk multiple texts
const batchResults = await chunker.chunkBatch(texts);
```

## Chunk Output

Every chunker returns `Chunk[]`:

```typescript
import { Chunk } from '@chonkiejs/core';

// Each chunk has:
chunk.text        // The chunk content
chunk.startIndex  // Start position in original text
chunk.endIndex    // End position in original text
chunk.tokenCount  // Token count
```

---

# recursive-chunker.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/chunkers/recursive-chunker.mdx

title: "RecursiveChunker"
description: "Hierarchical text chunking with customizable rules"

The `RecursiveChunker` splits text hierarchically using customizable rules. It's the most versatile chunker and works well for general-purpose text processing.

## How It Works

The chunker splits text through multiple levels:

1. **Paragraphs** — Split on `\n\n`, `\r\n`, `\n`, `\r`
2. **Sentences** — Split on `. `, `! `, `? `
3. **Punctuation** — Split on `{`, `}`, `(`, `)`, `,`, etc.
4. **Words** — Split on whitespace
5. **Characters** — Token-level splitting (final fallback)

Each level only activates if chunks from the previous level exceed `chunkSize`.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 512,
  minCharactersPerChunk: 24
});
```

## Parameters

| `chunkSize` | `number` | `512` | Maximum tokens per chunk |
| `minCharactersPerChunk` | `number` | `24` | Minimum characters when merging small splits |
| `rules` | `RecursiveRules` | Default rules | Custom chunking hierarchy |
| `tokenizer` | `Tokenizer` | Character tokenizer | Custom tokenizer instance |

## Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk('Your long document text...');

for (const chunk of chunks) {
  console.log(chunk.text);
  console.log(`Position: ${chunk.startIndex}-${chunk.endIndex}`);
  console.log(`Tokens: ${chunk.tokenCount}`);
}
```

## Custom Rules

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker, RecursiveRules } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const codeRules = new RecursiveRules({
  levels: [
    { delimiters: ['\n\n'] },           // Blank lines (blocks)
    { delimiters: ['\n'] },             // Single lines
    { delimiters: [';', '{', '}'] },    // Statements
    { whitespace: true },                // Words
    {}                                   // Characters
  ]
});

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 512,
  rules: codeRules
});

const chunks = await chunker.chunk(codeString);
```

## Batch Processing

```typescript
const texts = ['Document one...', 'Document two...'];
const batchResults = await chunker.chunkBatch(texts);

for (const [i, chunks] of batchResults.entries()) {
  console.log(`Document ${i + 1}: ${chunks.length} chunks`);
}
```

---

# semantic-chunker.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/chunkers/semantic-chunker.mdx

title: "SemanticChunker"
description: "Group content by semantic similarity"

The `SemanticChunker` groups text by semantic similarity using a custom embedding function. It keeps related content together in the same chunk.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { SemanticChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const embedFn = async (texts: string[]) => {
  // Your embedding logic here - return array of embeddings
  // Each embedding should be a number[]
};

const chunker = await SemanticChunker.create({
  embeddings: embedFn,
  threshold: 0.8,
  chunkSize: 2048,
  similarityWindow: 3,
});
```

## Parameters

| `embeddings` | `EmbedFunction \| EmbeddingModel` | required | Embedding function or object with `embed()` method |
| `threshold` | `number` | `0.8` | Similarity threshold (0-1). Lower = more splits |
| `chunkSize` | `number` | `2048` | Maximum tokens per chunk |
| `similarityWindow` | `number` | `3` | Number of sentences per sliding window embedding |

## Usage

```typescript
import { SemanticChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const embedFn = async (texts: string[]) => {
  // Call your embedding API here
  // e.g., OpenAI, Cohere, local model, etc.
  return texts.map(t => /* embedding vector */);
};

const chunker = await SemanticChunker.create({
  embeddings: embedFn,
  threshold: 0.7,
  chunkSize: 512
});

const text = "Your document text with multiple topics and themes...";
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(text);

for (const chunk of chunks) {
  console.log(`Chunk: ${chunk.text.slice(0, 50)}...`);
  console.log(`Tokens: ${chunk.tokenCount}`);
}
```

<Callout type="info">
The `embeddings` option accepts either a function `(texts: string[]) => Promise<number[][]>` or an object with an `embed(texts)` method. Each embedding vector should have the same dimensionality.
</Callout>

## With OpenAI Embeddings

```typescript
import { SemanticChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const openai = new OpenAI();

const embedFn = async (texts: string[]) => {
  const response = await openai.embeddings.create({
    model: 'text-embedding-3-small',
    input: texts,
  });
  return response.data.map(d => d.embedding);
};

const chunker = await SemanticChunker.create({
  embeddings: embedFn,
  threshold: 0.75,
  chunkSize: 1024
});
```

---

# sentence-chunker.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/chunkers/sentence-chunker.mdx

title: "SentenceChunker"
description: "Split text at sentence boundaries"

The `SentenceChunker` splits text at sentence boundaries, preserving semantic completeness at the sentence level.

| `chunkSize` | `number` | `512` | Maximum tokens per chunk |

| `minSentencesPerChunk` | `number` | `1` | Minimum sentences per chunk |

import { SentenceChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await SentenceChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 512,
  chunkOverlap: 128

# table-chunker.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/chunkers/table-chunker.mdx

title: "TableChunker"
description: "Chunk markdown/HTML tables by row or token count"

The `TableChunker` splits Markdown and HTML tables into smaller sub-tables while preserving the original table header in every chunk.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core
```

## Modes

The TableChunker supports two modes:

- **Row mode** (`tokenizer: 'row'`): `chunkSize` is the maximum number of data rows per chunk
- **Token mode**: `chunkSize` is the maximum token count per chunk

## Initialization

```typescript
import { TableChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

// Row mode (default): up to 3 data rows per chunk
const rowChunker = await TableChunker.create({
  tokenizer: 'row',
  chunkSize: 3
});

// Token mode: use tokenizer-based limits
const tokenChunker = await TableChunker.create({
  tokenizer: 'character',
  chunkSize: 512
});
```

## Parameters

| `tokenizer` | `Tokenizer \| 'row' \| string` | `'row'` | Chunking mode. `'row'` uses row-based chunking. |
| `chunkSize` | `number` | `3` | Max rows per chunk (row mode) or max tokens per chunk (token mode) |

## Usage

```typescript
import { TableChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const markdownTable = `
| Name | Age | City |
|------|-----|------|
| Alice | 30 | NYC |
| Bob | 25 | LA |
| Carol | 35 | Chicago |
| Dave | 28 | Boston |
| Eve | 32 | Seattle |
`.trim();

const chunker = await TableChunker.create({
  tokenizer: 'row',
  chunkSize: 2
});

const chunks = chunker.chunk(markdownTable);

for (const chunk of chunks) {
  console.log(chunk.text);
  console.log('---');
}
```

## Notes

- In row mode, `tokenCount` on output chunks represents the number of data rows in that chunk
- In token mode, `tokenCount` represents tokenizer-based token count
- Empty or invalid table input returns an empty array
- Headers are preserved in every chunk

---

# token-chunker.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/chunkers/token-chunker.mdx

title: "TokenChunker"
description: "Fixed-size token-based chunking"

The `TokenChunker` splits text into fixed-size token chunks. Best for maintaining consistent chunk sizes when working with token-based models.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { TokenChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await TokenChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 512,
  chunkOverlap: 128
});
```

## Parameters

| `chunkSize` | `number` | `512` | Maximum tokens per chunk |
| `chunkOverlap` | `number` | `128` | Number of overlapping tokens between chunks |
| `tokenizer` | `string` | `'character'` | Tokenizer to use (`'character'`, `'gpt2'`, or HuggingFace model name) |

## Usage

```typescript
import { TokenChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await TokenChunker.create({
  chunkSize: 512,
  chunkOverlap: 128
});

const text = "Your long document text...";
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(text);

for (const chunk of chunks) {
  console.log(`Chunk: ${chunk.text.slice(0, 50)}...`);
  console.log(`Tokens: ${chunk.tokenCount}`);
}
```

## With HuggingFace Tokenizer

For real token counting (requires `@chonkiejs/token`):

```typescript
import { TokenChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await TokenChunker.create({
  tokenizer: 'gpt2',
  chunkSize: 512,
  chunkOverlap: 128
});

const chunks = await chunker.chunk(text);
```

## Batch Processing

```typescript
const documents = ['Doc one...', 'Doc two...', 'Doc three...'];
const results = await chunker.chunkBatch(documents);
```

# installation.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/getting-started/installation.mdx

title: "Installation"
description: "Installing ChonkieJS packages"

ChonkieJS is distributed as multiple packages on npm. Install only what you need.

## Core Package

The core package includes all chunkers with zero runtime dependencies.

<Tabs items={["npm", "pnpm", "bun", "yarn"]}>
<Tab value="npm">
```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="pnpm">
```bash
pnpm add @chonkiejs/core
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="bun">
```bash
bun add @chonkiejs/core
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="yarn">
```bash
yarn add @chonkiejs/core
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Token Package

For HuggingFace tokenizer support (real token counting instead of character-based):

<Tabs items={["npm", "pnpm", "bun", "yarn"]}>
<Tab value="npm">
```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/token
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="pnpm">
```bash
pnpm add @chonkiejs/token
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="bun">
```bash
bun add @chonkiejs/token
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="yarn">
```bash
yarn add @chonkiejs/token
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Requirements

- Node.js 18+ (ESM support required)
- TypeScript 5.0+ (recommended for type safety)

<Callout type="info">
ChonkieJS is ESM-first. Make sure your project has `"type": "module"` in `package.json` or use `.mjs` file extensions.
</Callout>

# quick-start.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/getting-started/quick-start.mdx

title: "Quick Start"
description: "Get started with ChonkieJS in minutes"

## Install

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core
```

## Basic Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk('Your long document text...');

for (const chunk of chunks) {
  console.log(`[${chunk.startIndex}-${chunk.endIndex}]: ${chunk.text}`);
  console.log(`Tokens: ${chunk.tokenCount}`);
}
```

## Available Chunkers

```typescript
import {
  RecursiveChunker,
  TokenChunker,
  SentenceChunker,
  SemanticChunker,
  CodeChunker,
  TableChunker,
  FastChunker
} from '@chonkiejs/core';
```

Each chunker shares the same interface:

```typescript
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(text);        // Single text
const batch = await chunker.chunkBatch(texts);   // Multiple texts
```

## Chunk Output

Every chunker returns `Chunk[]` with consistent properties:

```typescript
interface Chunk {
  text: string;       // The chunk content
  startIndex: number; // Position in original text
  endIndex: number;   // End position in original text
  tokenCount: number; // Token count of the chunk
}
```

- Learn about each chunker in the [Chunkers](/chunkers/overview) section

# chroma.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/handshakes/chroma.mdx

title: "ChromaHandshake"
description: "Store and search chunks with ChromaDB"

The `ChromaHandshake` connects ChonkieJS to [ChromaDB](https://www.trychroma.com/), an open-source embedding database that runs in-memory or with persistent storage.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core chromadb
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { ChromaHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';
import { ChromaClient } from 'chromadb';

const client = new ChromaClient();
const collection = await client.getOrCreateCollection({
  name: 'my-docs',
  metadata: { 'hnsw:space': 'cosine' },
});

const handshake = new ChromaHandshake({
  collection,
  embeddings: async (texts) => embedModel.encode(texts),
});
```

## Parameters

| `collection` | `ChromaCollection` | — | Pre-initialized ChromaDB collection (must use cosine distance) |
| `embeddings` | `EmbedFunction \| EmbeddingModel` | — | Embedding function or model |
| `idPrefix` | `string` | `''` | Prefix for generated chunk IDs |

## Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker, ChromaHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(document);

// Store chunks
await handshake.write(chunks);

// Search
const results = await handshake.search('how do I reset my password?', {
  limit: 5,
});

for (const result of results) {
  console.log(`[${result.score.toFixed(3)}] ${result.text.slice(0, 80)}...`);
}
```

## Score Normalization

ChromaDB returns cosine **distance** (lower = more similar). The handshake converts this to a similarity score:

```
score = 1 - distance
```

A score of `1.0` means identical, `0.0` means orthogonal.

<Callout type="info">
Make sure your collection uses cosine distance (`hnsw:space = "cosine"`) for scores to be meaningful.
</Callout>

---

# elasticsearch.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/handshakes/elasticsearch.mdx

title: "ElasticHandshake"
description: "Store and search chunks with Elasticsearch"

The `ElasticHandshake` connects ChonkieJS to [Elasticsearch](https://www.elastic.co/elasticsearch), leveraging its dense vector field type for similarity search.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core @elastic/elasticsearch
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { ElasticHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';
import { Client } from '@elastic/elasticsearch';

const client = new Client({ node: 'http://localhost:9200' });

const handshake = new ElasticHandshake({
  client,
  indexName: 'my-docs',
  embeddings: async (texts) => embedModel.encode(texts),
});
```

## Parameters

| `client` | `ElasticClient` | — | Elasticsearch client instance |
| `indexName` | `string` | — | Name of the Elasticsearch index |
| `embeddings` | `EmbedFunction \| EmbeddingModel` | — | Embedding function or model |
| `idPrefix` | `string` | `''` | Prefix for generated chunk IDs |

## Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker, ElasticHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(document);

await handshake.write(chunks);

const results = await handshake.search('error handling patterns', { limit: 5 });

for (const result of results) {
  console.log(`[${result.score.toFixed(3)}] ${result.text.slice(0, 80)}...`);
}
```

<Callout type="info">
Create your index with a `dense_vector` field mapping before writing. Set `similarity: "cosine"` for normalized scores.
</Callout>

# lancedb.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/handshakes/lancedb.mdx

title: "LanceDBHandshake"
description: "Store and search chunks with LanceDB"

The `LanceDBHandshake` connects ChonkieJS to [LanceDB](https://lancedb.com/), a serverless columnar vector database with zero infrastructure overhead.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core @lancedb/lancedb
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { LanceDBHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';
import * as lancedb from '@lancedb/lancedb';

const db = await lancedb.connect('data/my-db');
const table = await db.openTable('chunks');

const handshake = new LanceDBHandshake({
  table,
  embeddings: async (texts) => embedModel.encode(texts),
});
```

## Parameters

| `table` | `LanceTable` | — | Pre-initialized LanceDB table |
| `embeddings` | `EmbedFunction \| EmbeddingModel` | — | Embedding function or model |
| `idPrefix` | `string` | `''` | Prefix for generated chunk IDs |

## Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker, LanceDBHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(document);

await handshake.write(chunks);

const results = await handshake.search('deployment configuration', { limit: 5 });

for (const result of results) {
  console.log(`[${result.score.toFixed(3)}] ${result.text.slice(0, 80)}...`);
}
```

## Score Normalization

LanceDB returns Euclidean distance by default. The handshake converts to similarity:

```
score = 1 / (1 + distance)
```

# milvus.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/handshakes/milvus.mdx

title: "MilvusHandshake"
description: "Store and search chunks with Milvus"

The `MilvusHandshake` connects ChonkieJS to [Milvus](https://milvus.io/), a scalable open-source vector database built for billion-scale similarity search.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core @zilliz/milvus2-sdk-node
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { MilvusHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';
import { MilvusClient } from '@zilliz/milvus2-sdk-node';

const client = new MilvusClient({ address: 'localhost:19530' });

const handshake = new MilvusHandshake({
  client,
  collectionName: 'my_docs',
  embeddings: async (texts) => embedModel.encode(texts),
});
```

## Parameters

| `client` | `MilvusClient` | — | Pre-initialized Milvus client |
| `collectionName` | `string` | — | Name of the Milvus collection |
| `embeddings` | `EmbedFunction \| EmbeddingModel` | — | Embedding function or model |
| `idPrefix` | `string` | `''` | Prefix for generated chunk IDs |

## Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker, MilvusHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(document);

await handshake.write(chunks);

const results = await handshake.search('machine learning models', { limit: 5 });

for (const result of results) {
  console.log(`[${result.score.toFixed(3)}] ${result.text.slice(0, 80)}...`);
}
```

<Callout type="info">
Ensure your Milvus collection schema includes a vector field with the correct dimension for your embedding model.
</Callout>

---

# mongodb.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/handshakes/mongodb.mdx

title: "MongoDBHandshake"
description: "Store and search chunks with MongoDB Atlas Vector Search"

The `MongoDBHandshake` connects ChonkieJS to [MongoDB Atlas Vector Search](https://www.mongodb.com/products/platform/atlas-vector-search), enabling similarity search on chunks stored in MongoDB collections.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core mongodb
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { MongoDBHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';
import { MongoClient } from 'mongodb';

const client = new MongoClient(process.env.MONGODB_URI);
await client.connect();
const collection = client.db('mydb').collection('chunks');

const handshake = new MongoDBHandshake({
  collection,
  indexName: 'vector_index',
  embeddings: async (texts) => embedModel.encode(texts),
});
```

## Parameters

| `collection` | `MongoCollection` | — | MongoDB collection instance |
| `indexName` | `string` | `'default'` | Atlas Vector Search index name |
| `embeddings` | `EmbedFunction \| EmbeddingModel` | — | Embedding function or model |
| `idPrefix` | `string` | `''` | Prefix for generated chunk IDs |

## Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker, MongoDBHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(document);

await handshake.write(chunks);

const results = await handshake.search('billing questions', { limit: 5 });

for (const result of results) {
  console.log(`[${result.score.toFixed(3)}] ${result.text.slice(0, 80)}...`);
}
```

<Callout type="info">
You must create an Atlas Vector Search index on the `embedding` field before searching. See the [Atlas documentation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-vector-search/create-index/) for setup instructions.
</Callout>

# overview.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/handshakes/overview.mdx

title: "Handshakes Overview"
description: "Vector database integrations for storing and searching chunks"

Handshakes are ChonkieJS's adapter layer for vector databases. They provide a unified interface to store chunks with their embeddings and perform similarity search across 10 supported backends.

## How It Works

1. **Chunk** your text with any chunker
2. **Initialize** a handshake with your vector DB client and an embedding function
3. **Write** chunks — embeddings are computed and stored automatically
4. **Search** by text query or raw embedding vector

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker, ChromaHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(document);

const handshake = new ChromaHandshake({
  collection: myChromaCollection,
  embeddings: async (texts) => embedModel.encode(texts),
});

await handshake.write(chunks);

const results = await handshake.search('what is the return policy?');
```

## Available Handshakes

<Cards>
  <Card title="ChromaHandshake" href="/handshakes/chroma">
    ChromaDB — in-memory or persistent local vector store.
  </Card>
  <Card title="PineconeHandshake" href="/handshakes/pinecone">
    Pinecone — fully managed cloud vector database.
  </Card>
  <Card title="QdrantHandshake" href="/handshakes/qdrant">
    Qdrant — open-source vector search engine.
  </Card>
  <Card title="WeaviateHandshake" href="/handshakes/weaviate">
    Weaviate — AI-native vector database.
  </Card>
  <Card title="MilvusHandshake" href="/handshakes/milvus">
    Milvus — scalable open-source vector DB.
  </Card>
  <Card title="MongoDBHandshake" href="/handshakes/mongodb">
    MongoDB Atlas Vector Search.
  </Card>
  <Card title="ElasticHandshake" href="/handshakes/elasticsearch">
    Elasticsearch with vector search support.
  </Card>
  <Card title="LanceDBHandshake" href="/handshakes/lancedb">
    LanceDB — serverless columnar vector database.
  </Card>
  <Card title="TurbopufferHandshake" href="/handshakes/turbopuffer">
    Turbopuffer — edge-optimized vector search.
  </Card>
  <Card title="PgvectorHandshake" href="/handshakes/pgvector">
    PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension.
  </Card>
</Cards>

## Common Interface

All handshakes implement the same four methods:

```typescript
// Store chunks with their embeddings
await handshake.write(chunks);

// Search by text query (embedding computed internally)
const results = await handshake.search('query text', { limit: 10 });

// Search by pre-computed embedding vector
const results = await handshake.searchByVector(embedding, { limit: 10 });

// Get total stored chunk count
const total = await handshake.count();
```

## Search Results

Every search returns `HandshakeSearchResult[]`:

```typescript
interface HandshakeSearchResult {
  id: string;         // Deterministic SHA256-based ID
  score: number;      // Similarity score (0–1, higher is better)
  text: string;       // Original chunk text
  startIndex: number; // Start position in source document
  endIndex: number;   // End position in source document
  tokenCount: number; // Token count of the chunk
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

## Embeddings

Handshakes accept an embedding function in two forms:

```typescript
// Function form
const handshake = new ChromaHandshake({
  collection,
  embeddings: async (texts: string[]) => {
    return await myModel.encode(texts); // returns number[][]
  },
});

// Object form (must have an `embed` method)
const handshake = new ChromaHandshake({
  collection,
  embeddings: myEmbeddingModel, // { embed(texts: string[]): Promise<number[][]> }
});
```

## ID Generation

Chunk IDs are deterministic — writing the same chunk twice won't create duplicates. IDs are generated as:

```
SHA256(idPrefix + startIndex + ":" + endIndex + ":" + text).slice(0, 32)
```

Use `idPrefix` to namespace IDs when storing chunks from multiple documents in the same collection:

```typescript
const handshake = new PineconeHandshake({
  index: myIndex,
  embeddings: embed,
  idPrefix: 'doc-123/',
});
```

---

# pgvector.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/handshakes/pgvector.mdx

title: "PgvectorHandshake"
description: "Store and search chunks with PostgreSQL and pgvector"

The `PgvectorHandshake` connects ChonkieJS to PostgreSQL using the [pgvector](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector) extension, letting you store and search embeddings alongside your relational data.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core pg
```

Make sure the `pgvector` extension is installed on your PostgreSQL instance:

```sql
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { PgvectorHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';
import { Pool } from 'pg';

const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL });

const handshake = new PgvectorHandshake({
  client: pool,
  tableName: 'document_chunks',
  embeddings: async (texts) => embedModel.encode(texts),
});
```

## Parameters

| `client` | `PgClient` | — | A `pg` Pool or Client instance |
| `tableName` | `string` | `'chunks'` | Table name for storing chunks |
| `autoCreateTable` | `boolean` | `true` | Auto-create table on first write |
| `embeddings` | `EmbedFunction \| EmbeddingModel` | — | Embedding function or model |
| `idPrefix` | `string` | `''` | Prefix for generated chunk IDs |

## Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker, PgvectorHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(document);

await handshake.write(chunks);

const results = await handshake.search('order tracking', { limit: 5 });

for (const result of results) {
  console.log(`[${result.score.toFixed(3)}] ${result.text.slice(0, 80)}...`);
}
```

## Auto Table Creation

By default, the handshake creates the table on the first `write()` call:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS document_chunks (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  text TEXT NOT NULL,
  start_index INTEGER NOT NULL,
  end_index INTEGER NOT NULL,
  token_count INTEGER NOT NULL,
  embedding vector(1536)  -- dimension inferred from first embedding
)
```

Set `autoCreateTable: false` if you want to manage the schema yourself.

## Upsert Behavior

Writes use `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE`, so writing the same chunk twice updates it in place rather than throwing a duplicate key error.

## Score Computation

Similarity is computed using cosine distance (`<=>` operator):

```
score = 1 - (embedding <=> query_vector)
```

Results are ordered by cosine distance ascending (most similar first).

---

# pinecone.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/handshakes/pinecone.mdx

title: "PineconeHandshake"
description: "Store and search chunks with Pinecone"

The `PineconeHandshake` connects ChonkieJS to [Pinecone](https://www.pinecone.io/), a fully managed cloud vector database.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core @pinecone-database/pinecone
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { PineconeHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';
import { Pinecone } from '@pinecone-database/pinecone';

const pc = new Pinecone({ apiKey: process.env.PINECONE_API_KEY });
const index = pc.index('my-index');

const handshake = new PineconeHandshake({
  index,
  namespace: 'documents',
  embeddings: async (texts) => embedModel.encode(texts),
});
```

## Parameters

| `index` | `PineconeIndex` | — | Pre-initialized Pinecone index instance |
| `namespace` | `string` | `''` | Namespace within the index |
| `embeddings` | `EmbedFunction \| EmbeddingModel` | — | Embedding function or model |
| `idPrefix` | `string` | `''` | Prefix for generated chunk IDs |

## Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker, PineconeHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(document);

// Store chunks (batched in groups of 100 automatically)
await handshake.write(chunks);

// Search
const results = await handshake.search('quarterly revenue', { limit: 5 });

for (const result of results) {
  console.log(`[${result.score.toFixed(3)}] ${result.text.slice(0, 80)}...`);
}
```

## Batch Writes

Pinecone has a 100-vector upsert limit per request. The handshake handles batching internally — you can pass thousands of chunks to `write()` without worrying about limits.

## Namespaces

Use namespaces to partition data within a single index:

```typescript
const docsHandshake = new PineconeHandshake({
  index,
  namespace: 'docs',
  embeddings: embed,
});

const faqHandshake = new PineconeHandshake({
  index,
  namespace: 'faq',
  embeddings: embed,
});
```

The `count()` method returns the record count for the configured namespace (or the total index count if no namespace is set).

---

# qdrant.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/handshakes/qdrant.mdx

title: "QdrantHandshake"
description: "Store and search chunks with Qdrant"

The `QdrantHandshake` connects ChonkieJS to [Qdrant](https://qdrant.tech/), an open-source vector search engine with filtering and payload support.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core @qdrant/js-client-rest
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { QdrantHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';
import { QdrantClient } from '@qdrant/js-client-rest';

const client = new QdrantClient({ url: 'http://localhost:6333' });

const handshake = new QdrantHandshake({
  client,
  collectionName: 'my-docs',
  embeddings: async (texts) => embedModel.encode(texts),
});
```

## Parameters

| `client` | `QdrantClient` | — | Pre-initialized Qdrant client |
| `collectionName` | `string` | — | Name of the Qdrant collection |
| `embeddings` | `EmbedFunction \| EmbeddingModel` | — | Embedding function or model |
| `idPrefix` | `string` | `''` | Prefix for generated chunk IDs |

## Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker, QdrantHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(document);

await handshake.write(chunks);

const results = await handshake.search('authentication flow', { limit: 5 });

for (const result of results) {
  console.log(`[${result.score.toFixed(3)}] ${result.text.slice(0, 80)}...`);
}
```

<Callout type="info">
Make sure the Qdrant collection is created with cosine distance before using the handshake. The collection's vector dimension must match your embedding model's output.
</Callout>

# turbopuffer.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/handshakes/turbopuffer.mdx

title: "TurbopufferHandshake"
description: "Store and search chunks with Turbopuffer"

The `TurbopufferHandshake` connects ChonkieJS to [Turbopuffer](https://turbopuffer.com/), an edge-optimized vector search service designed for low-latency queries.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core @turbopuffer/turbopuffer
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { TurbopufferHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';
import { Turbopuffer } from '@turbopuffer/turbopuffer';

const tpuf = new Turbopuffer({ apiKey: process.env.TURBOPUFFER_API_KEY });
const namespace = tpuf.namespace('my-docs');

const handshake = new TurbopufferHandshake({
  namespace,
  embeddings: async (texts) => embedModel.encode(texts),
});
```

## Parameters

| `namespace` | `TurbopufferNamespace` | — | Pre-initialized Turbopuffer namespace |
| `embeddings` | `EmbedFunction \| EmbeddingModel` | — | Embedding function or model |
| `idPrefix` | `string` | `''` | Prefix for generated chunk IDs |

## Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker, TurbopufferHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(document);

await handshake.write(chunks);

const results = await handshake.search('user preferences', { limit: 5 });

for (const result of results) {
  console.log(`[${result.score.toFixed(3)}] ${result.text.slice(0, 80)}...`);
}
```

## Score Normalization

Turbopuffer returns distance values. The handshake converts to similarity:

```
score = 1 - distance
```

# weaviate.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/handshakes/weaviate.mdx

title: "WeaviateHandshake"
description: "Store and search chunks with Weaviate"

The `WeaviateHandshake` connects ChonkieJS to [Weaviate](https://weaviate.io/), an AI-native vector database with built-in vectorization and hybrid search.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @chonkiejs/core weaviate-client
```

## Initialization

```typescript
import { WeaviateHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';
import weaviate from 'weaviate-client';

const client = await weaviate.connectToLocal();
const collection = client.collections.get('MyDocs');

const handshake = new WeaviateHandshake({
  collection,
  embeddings: async (texts) => embedModel.encode(texts),
});
```

## Parameters

| `collection` | `WeaviateCollection` | — | Pre-initialized Weaviate collection |
| `embeddings` | `EmbedFunction \| EmbeddingModel` | — | Embedding function or model |
| `idPrefix` | `string` | `''` | Prefix for generated chunk IDs |

## Usage

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker, WeaviateHandshake } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk(document);

await handshake.write(chunks);

const results = await handshake.search('data processing pipeline', { limit: 5 });

for (const result of results) {
  console.log(`[${result.score.toFixed(3)}] ${result.text.slice(0, 80)}...`);
}
```

## Score Normalization

Weaviate returns distance values. The handshake converts to similarity:

```
score = 1 - distance
```

# index.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/index.mdx

title: "ChonkieJS"
description: "The lightweight JavaScript chunking library for RAG pipelines"

ChonkieJS is the JavaScript/TypeScript implementation of [Chonkie](https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkie) — bringing fast, efficient text chunking to the JavaScript ecosystem.

## Features

<Cards>
  <Card title="Zero Dependencies">
    @chonkiejs/core has no runtime dependencies — lightweight and fast.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Multiple Chunkers">
    Token, Recursive, Sentence, Semantic, Code, Table, and Fast chunkers included.
  </Card>
  <Card title="TypeScript Native">
    Full TypeScript type definitions with ESM-first design.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Async API">
    All chunkers support async/await for non-blocking pipelines.
  </Card>
</Cards>

## Packages

| Package | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `@chonkiejs/core` | Core chunking library with all chunkers |
| `@chonkiejs/token` | HuggingFace tokenizer support |

## Quick Example

```typescript
import { RecursiveChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 512 });
const chunks = await chunker.chunk('Your long document text...');

for (const chunk of chunks) {
  console.log(chunk.text);
  console.log(`Tokens: ${chunk.tokenCount}`);
}
```

# troubleshooting.mdx

Source: https://github.com/chonkie-inc/chonkiejs/blob/main/docs/content/docs/troubleshooting.mdx

title: "Troubleshooting"
description: "Solutions to common issues when using ChonkieJS"
icon: LifeBuoy

Having trouble? Check the common issues below. If your problem isn't listed, reach out on [Discord](https://discord.gg/Q6zkP8w6ur).

## Installation Issues

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="Cannot find module '@chonkiejs/core'">
    Make sure you've installed the package:

    ```bash
    npm install @chonkiejs/core
    ```

    If you're using a monorepo, ensure the package is hoisted or listed in the correct workspace's `package.json`.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="ERR_REQUIRE_ESM or 'import' errors">
    ChonkieJS is an ESM-only package. Make sure your project is configured for ESM:

    - Add `"type": "module"` to your `package.json`, OR
    - Use `.mjs` file extensions, OR
    - Use dynamic `import()` instead of `require()`

    ```json
    {
      "type": "module"
    }
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="TypeScript compilation errors">
    Ensure your `tsconfig.json` uses a modern module resolution:

    ```json
    {
      "compilerOptions": {
        "module": "ESNext",
        "moduleResolution": "bundler",
        "target": "ES2020"
      }
    }
    ```
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Chunking Issues

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="My chunks are too small">
    Increase `chunkSize`. The value represents the maximum token count per chunk.

    ```typescript
    const chunker = await RecursiveChunker.create({ chunkSize: 1024 });
    ```

    Common values:
    - **256** — tight context windows, Q&A bots
    - **512** — balanced default for most RAG pipelines
    - **1024+** — longer documents, summarization tasks
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="My chunks are too large">
    If chunks exceed your expected size:

    1. `chunkSize` is in **tokens**, not characters
    2. Some chunkers (SentenceChunker, RecursiveChunker) won't split mid-sentence
    3. For strict limits, use `TokenChunker` which guarantees the size constraint
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="SemanticChunker requires an embedding function">
    SemanticChunker needs you to provide an `embeddings` function that maps text to vectors:

    ```typescript
    import { SemanticChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

    const chunker = await SemanticChunker.create({
      chunkSize: 512,
      threshold: 0.5,
      embeddings: async (texts: string[]) => {
        // Call your embedding API here
        // Must return number[][] (one vector per input text)
        const response = await fetch('your-embedding-api', {
          method: 'POST',
          body: JSON.stringify({ inputs: texts })
        });
        return response.json();
      }
    });
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="CodeChunker produces empty chunks or errors">
    Common causes:

    1. **Wrong language** — make sure the `language` parameter matches your file (`"typescript"`, `"python"`, etc.)
    2. **Invalid syntax** — the AST parser can't handle files with syntax errors
    3. **Very small files** — if the file is smaller than `chunkSize`, you get a single chunk
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="FastChunker cuts in the middle of words">
    Expected behavior. FastChunker splits on byte boundaries for maximum throughput. Use `RecursiveChunker` or `SentenceChunker` if you need clean word/sentence boundaries.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Integration Issues

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="Embedding dimension mismatch with vector DB">
    Your embedding function's output dimension must match your vector database's configured dimension.

    Common dimensions:
    - OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`: 1536
    - Cohere `embed-english-v3`: 1024
    - Local models vary — check your model's docs

    Verify your handshake was created with the correct dimension:

    ```typescript
    const handshake = new QdrantHandshake({
      collectionName: 'my-docs',
      dimension: 1536, // Must match your embedding output
    });
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Handshake connection errors">
    Verify:

    1. Your vector DB is running and accessible
    2. API keys are correct
    3. The collection/index exists (check your DB's dashboard)
    4. Network allows the connection (CORS for browser, firewall for server)
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Memory issues with large documents">
    For very large documents:

    1. **Pre-split** — divide into sections before chunking
    2. **Process sequentially** — avoid loading all chunks into memory at once
    3. **Stream to vector DB** — write chunks as they're produced

    ```typescript
    // Process in batches
    const sections = splitLargeText(document, 100_000);
    for (const section of sections) {
      const chunks = await chunker.chunk(section);
      await handshake.write(chunks);
    }
    ```
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Tokenizer Issues

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="Custom tokenizer not counting tokens correctly">
    If you're providing a custom tokenizer, make sure it returns accurate token counts. The chunkers rely on these counts to respect `chunkSize`:

    ```typescript
    import { TokenChunker } from '@chonkiejs/core';

    const chunker = await TokenChunker.create({
      chunkSize: 512,
      tokenizer: {
        encode: (text) => /* must return token array */,
        decode: (tokens) => /* must return string */,
      }
    });
    ```

    Test your tokenizer independently to verify counts match expectations.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

---
